15 	
16 	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
17 	
18 	## What "instant" means
19 	
20 	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
21 	
22 	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
23 	
24 	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
25 	
26 	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
27 	
28 	<details>
29 	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
30 	
31 	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
32 	
33 	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
34 	
35 	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
36 	
37 	</details>
38 	
39 	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.
40 	
41 	## Quick start
42 	
43 	Getting the most out of Instant Navigation requires enabling [Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), then following the [validation errors](#validate-instant-navigation) that appear:
44 	
45 	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
46 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
47 	
48 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
49 	  cacheComponents: true,
50 	  partialPrefetching: true,
51 	}
52 	
53 	export default nextConfig
54 	```

Everything is in place and verified. Here's a summary of what I implemented, following the patterns from the Next.js 16 view-transitions guide (node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/view-transitions.md):

## Changes

### 1. Shared element morph (thumbnail → hero image)
- app/ProductGrid.tsx — Each grid thumbnail is wrapped in <ViewTransition name={product-${slug}} share="morph" default="none">.
- app/product/[slug]/page.tsx — The detail hero image is wrapped in a matching <ViewTransition name={product-${slug}} share="morph" default="none">.

React finds the two elements with the same name on the old and new pages and the browser animates the size/position morph automatically. share="morph" assigns the morph view-transition-class (targeted in CSS with a mid-flight blur to hide interpolation artifacts), and default="none" prevents the named pair from crossfading on unrelated transitions.

### 2. Suspense loading reveal (skeleton → content)
- app/product/[slug]/page.tsx — The DetailsSkeleton fallback is wrapped in <ViewTransition exit="slide-down" default="none"> and the ProductDetails content in <ViewTransition enter="slide-up" default="none">.

The skeleton slides down and fades out (fast 150ms exit), then the real content slides up and fades in (slower 210ms fade delayed until the exit completes, 400ms slide). Defined in CSS via ::view-transition-old(.slide-down) / ::view-transition-new(.slide-up).

### 3. Directional page navigation slides
- Grid links use transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}; the back link uses transitionTypes={['nav-back']}.
- Both app/page.tsx and app/product/[slug]/page.tsx wrap their page content in a <ViewTransition> with enter/exit objects keyed by nav-forward and nav-back (with default: "none" so untyped navigations like browser back/forward and Suspense reveals don't get a directional slide).

Forward navigation slides content left; back navigation slides content right (60px offset). The wrapper is in each page.tsx, not the layout, because layouts persist across navigations so enter/exit never fire there.

### 4. prefers-reduced-motion
- app/globals.css — A @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block sets animation-duration: 0s and animation-delay: 0s on all ::view-transition-old(), ::view-transition-new(), and ::view-transition-group() pseudo-elements, so all transitions complete instantly for users who prefer reduced motion.

### Supporting CSS
Added ::view-transition { pointer-events: none; } so the page stays clickable during transitions, plus all the keyframes (via-blur, fade, slide-y, slide) and timing variables from the guide.

### Verification
- tsc --noEmit — passed (exit 0)
- npm run build — passed (exit 0), all 3 routes generated successfully

One note: the morph plays when the destination content renders in the same commit as the navigation (i.e., prefetched/cached pages). If the destination suspends into a fallback first, no pair forms and the content animates with its enter animation instead when it arrives — this is expected behavior per the guide.
